meaning:
παρά-δοσις, -εως, ἡ
(παραδίδωμι), [in LXX: Est.7:26 (אֵסוּר), Jer.32:4 (נָתַן ni.), Jer.34:2 * ;]
1. a handing down or over, transfer, transmission (Arist., Polyb., al., LXX).
2. tradition of doctrine (Plat., Epict., al.); by meton., of the doctrine itself : Mat.15:2-3, 6, Mrk.7:3, 1Co.11:2, Gal.1:14, Col.2:8, 2Th.2:15 3:9.†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: “Why do your disciples disobey the tradition of the elders? For they don’t wash their hands when they eat bread.”
(For the Pharisees and all the Jews don’t eat unless they wash their hands and forearms, holding to the tradition of the elders.
Now I praise you, brothers, that you remember me in all things, and hold firm the traditions, even as I delivered them to you.
I advanced in the Jews’ religion beyond many of my own age among my countrymen, being more exceedingly zealous for the traditions of my fathers.
Be careful that you don’t let anyone rob you through his philosophy and vain deceit, after the tradition of men, after the elements of the world, and not after…
So then, brothers, stand firm and hold the traditions which you were taught by us, whether by word or by letter.
